articles.title: Southern India's First Barrier Free Toll Plazas Are Now Live! - Cartoq
articles.content: Southern India's First Barrier Free Toll Plazas Are Now Live [Video] Written By: Neeraj Padmakumar Published: November 14, 2026 at 12:55 PM Updated: November 14, 2026 at 12:55 PM The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) is rolling out the barrier-free tolling system in more parts of the country in a phased manner. The authority has now set up the first Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) tolling systems in southern India, and interestingly, they are both in Tamil Nadu. The first is the Paranur toll plaza and the second is the Nemili plaza. The MLFF system allows vehicles to pass through without having to stop to pay the toll. This system works based on cameras and FASTag technology. Paranur Toll Plaza Was The First NHAI introduced the MLFF system at the Paranur Toll Plaza on October 1, 2026. Located near Chengalpattu on the 46.5-km Tambaram-Tindivanam section of National Highway 45. It became Tamil Nadu's first toll plaza to adopt the fully-automated toll collection system. Vehicles travelling along this stretch no longer had top stop at the plaza to make payments. Overhead equipment reads the vehicle's FASTag and captures its registration number as it passes through the tolling zone. Payment is processed automatically based on this data. India’s first MLFF tolling setup was introduced on the Kamrej-Choryasi section between Surat and Bharuch in Gujarat in May 2026. Paranur’s installation followed this. NHAI is working on introducing barrier-free tolling on more roads in parts of Delhi, Haryana and Rajasthan. Nemili Toll Plaza Gets Barrier-Free Tolling Tamil Nadu’s second and NHAI’s latest installation of the MLFF system is at the Nemili plaza. It is on the Sriperumbudur-Karaipettai section of National Highway 48. It was taken operational on November 13, 2026. Here too, the system uses advanced electronic equipment and technologies to identify vehicles and charge toll as they pass through the tolling zone. A press release put out by PIB Chennai claims that the MLFF system can effectively curtail traffic congestion by minimising the need for human intervention. This can, in the larger picture, reduce travel time, fuel consumption and emissions. It also claims that operational efficiencies are further heightened through optimized lane throughput and reduced physical infrastructure overheads. The authority has advised motorists to keep their FASTags valid and ensure they have sufficient balance in them. Vehicles with insufficient balance or an invalid or non-functional FASTag may receive e-notices. What Is The MLFF Tolling System And How Does It Work? Multi-Lane Free Flow is a barrier-free toll collection technology that allows vehicles to pass through tolling points without stopping or entering a dedicated toll lane. It uses a combination of Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR), FASTag-based Electronic Toll Collection (ETC) and other vehicle-detection technologies. As a vehicle approaches the tolling zone, overhead cameras capture its registration number while the FASTag system reads the tag using radio-frequency identification (RFID). The information is then used to identify the vehicle and process the applicable toll charge automatically. Some advanced MLFF installations also use LiDAR technology. Short...

articles.title: PM Modi Opens India's First LED Dome Planetarium - UdaipurTimes.com
articles.content: PM Modi Opens India's First LED Dome Planetarium COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium, in Mysuru, is India's first LED dome planetarium By Razia Sanwari | Nov 14, 2026, 12:17 IST Join for live updates on WhatsApp UdaipurTimes, Nov 14, 2026 - Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday, November 13, inaugurated the country's first LED dome planetarium - the COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium - in Mysuru, Karnataka. Addressing the gathering on the occasion, the Prime Minister expressed his delight at returning to Mysuru to dedicate the COSMOS Planetarium to the Nation just months after inaugurating the Viveka Smaraka. He pointed out that while the Viveka Smaraka inspires introspection and spiritual pursuit, the COSMOS Planetarium directs the gaze skyward to unravel the mysteries of the vast universe and he emphasised the profound cultural message conveyed by both landmarks. “This is an example of the fact that in India, the traditions of spirituality and science have always moved forward together,” the Prime Minister said. Highlighting Mysuru's rich tradition of fostering knowledge institutions, including the establishment of the University of Mysore under Maharaja Nalwadi Krishnaraja Wadiyar and the Wadiyar Royal Family's pivotal role in laying the foundation of the Indian Institute of Science in Bengaluru to empower generations of scholars, the Prime Minister noted that Mysuru is adding a new chapter to India's scientific journey with the dedication of this state-of-the-art planetarium to the youth and citizens. PM Modi highlighted the government's decision to open the space sector to private participation, which has enabled Indian startups and youth to showcase their capabilities by launching private rockets, placing satellites into orbit and undertaking unprecedented space ventures. Stating that advancing research requires giving students and scholars access to the world's finest scientific literature, the Prime Minister mentioned the launch of One Nation One Subscription to help domestic institutes access leading global journals alongside the creation of the Anusandhan National Research Foundation. The Prime Minister concluded his address by urging those associated with COSMOS to continuously invite school and college students from across the region and extended his best wishes for the journey ahead. “The children who come here to learn about the universe, it is possible that some of them may return here one day and tell us what new discoveries they have made about the universe, and this alone will be the biggest success of this COSMOS Planetarium,” PM Modi said. articles.title: PM Modi hails COSMOS, calls it extraordinary experience - The New Indian Express
articles.content: MYSURU: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday said the state-of-the-art COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium would inspire young minds to explore the mysteries of the universe and contribute to India’s growing scientific achievements. Speaking after dedicating COSMOS-Mysuru, India’s first LED Dome Planetarium, to the nation, Modi said the facility would add a new chapter to India’s scientific journey and provide students and researchers with opportunities to develop scientific curiosity and pursue new discoveries. Drawing a parallel between the Viveka Smaraka, which he had inaugurated in Mysuru recently, and COSMOS-Mysuru, Modi said the two institutions conveyed a profound message about India’s traditions of spirituality and science. While Viveka Smaraka inspired people to look within and seek spiritual knowledge, COSMOS encouraged them to look towards the skies and understand the vast universe. “India’s traditions of spirituality and science have always progressed together,” he said, recalling the contributions of ancient Indian astronomers Aryabhata, Varahamihira, Bhaskaracharya and Neelakantha Somayaji, who made significant discoveries and complex calculations without modern instruments and technology. Speaking of Mysuru’s legacy of promoting education and research, he recalled that the University of Mysore was established during the reign of Nalwadi Krishnaraja Wadiyar and the Wadiyar family played an important role in laying the foundation for the Indian Institute of Science in Bengaluru. Congratulating the Indian Institute of Astrophysics, University of Mysore, government departments and those associated with the project, Modi described COSMOS as an extraordinary experience. Referring to India’s achievements in international science competitions, he said five Indian students participated in the International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics in Vietnam this year, four won gold medals and one got silver. “When young people are provided with opportunities, resources, technology, tools and institutional support, they achieve remarkable milestones,” Modi said. Highlighting India’s progress in space exploration over the past decade, Modi cited the successful Chandrayaan-3 mission and Aditya-L1 solar observatory. He said the opening up of the space sector had created new opportunities for private companies and startups, enabling young entrepreneurs to develop rockets, launch satellites and undertake activities previously unprecedented in India. Similarly, real-time train tracking systems developed by Railways and ISRO enabled passengers to check train locations and arrival times. Satellite data was also being used to estimate crop yields and determine insurance claims, he said. “Science for Society is our approach. Satellites are reaching new heights in space, and improving the lives of people on Earth,” he added. Referring to the `1 lakh crore Research, Development and Innovation scheme launched last year, Modi said it would ensure adequate funding for researchers and help translate new technologies into practical applications. He called for greater participation of school and college students at COSMOS. “Some of the children who visit COSMOS today may return one day with new discoveries about the universe. That will be the greatest success of this planetarium,” he said. Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

articles.title: Mysuru Planetarium Opens as India's First LED Curved-Dome Facility - Urban Acres
articles.content: Home Breaking News Mysuru Planetarium Opens as India’s First LED Curved-Dome Facility Breaking News Mysuru Planetarium Opens as India’s First LED Curved-Dome Facility By Maria Dsouza November 14, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Mysuru planetarium described as India’s first LED curved-dome planetarium, along with the Cosmos–Mysuru cosmology education and research training centre, at the foothills of Chamundi Hill on Friday. The facilities have been built by the Union Department of Science and Technology and are intended to expand public access to astronomy education and research training. Speaking at a public function after the inauguration, Modi said science and innovation were being consistently encouraged to support society and development. He described the planetarium as a new chapter in India’s scientific journey and said it could help give shape to the aspirations of young people. The Prime Minister visited the planetarium and was briefed on its advanced facilities. He also viewed space-related presentations from the facility’s “Sky Theatre” and interacted with children. Describing the experience as “truly wonderful”, Modi said a visit to the planetarium could turn people’s attention towards the sky and encourage them to understand the wider universe and its unanswered questions. The project combines a public-facing astronomy venue with the Cosmos–Mysuru centre, which is focused on cosmology education and research training. The source report does not specify the total project cost, seating capacity, operating schedule or the number of students and visitors the facility is expected to serve. At the event, Modi linked the new facility to Mysuru’s longer educational history. He referred to the establishment of the University of Mysore during the period of Nalvadi Krishnaraja Wadiyar and the role of the Wadiyar family in the establishment of the Indian Institute of Science in Bengaluru. He said these institutions had provided generations of students and researchers with opportunities to develop their abilities and pursue new work. The Prime Minister also highlighted the government’s decision to open the space sector to private participation, saying this had created new opportunities for private industry and a platform for Indian start-ups to demonstrate their capabilities. He said satellite technology, space science and earth-science technologies were being combined to improve everyday life. Research access was another theme of the address. Modi said students and researchers needed access to high-quality research facilities and scientific publications, and referred to the One Nation One Subscription initiative as a measure launched for that purpose. The report does not provide further operational details about how the initiative will be linked to the Cosmos–Mysuru centre. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, Governor Sudha Yadav, Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, Higher Education Minister Basavaraj Rayareddi and Mysuru-Kodagu MP Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar attended the programme. The new planetarium adds a specialised science-education facility to Mysuru’s institutional landscape, while its longer public impact will depend on access, programming and the scale of its engagement with schools, students and researchers.
